minutes.headline: Select Board heard a preliminary Municipal Building plan and the assessment consultant's report, and denied the 243 Summer Street paving request.
minutes.summary: The board heard a presentation from the Municipal Building Design Committee on a hybrid plan for Ritter, Town Hall and the old TCP building, with preliminary comparative costs. It heard the consultant's report on waterfront land valuation and the board of assessors' abatement process, and members sharply criticized the assessors. The board approved a toll booth fundraiser and the fourth-quarter water commitment, denied the 243 Summer Street request, and reviewed its FY23 goals.

public_comment.topic: A departing official thanked supporters of nine years in office and urged residents to vote in Saturday's town election.
Asked whether the public could ask questions after the building design committee presentation.

Asked about the school versus town split of space in the Ritter building and suggested making the meeting room into offices instead of building an addition; called it a lot of money for community space.
Thanked the consultant and criticized the assessment errors and the length of the abatement ordeal for residents.
Argued the combined square footage and cost for community space is too high; suggested splitting the school and town offices and noted Pepperell converted a meeting room into offices.

votes.motion: Approve the Lunenburg Boys and Girls Club toll booth fundraiser on Saturday June 3rd, 9 A.M. to 1 P.M. at Town Center.
Commit the fourth quarter water commitment.
Deny the request of the residents at 243 Summer Street as presented.

budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee's letter attached a map of a proposed sidewalk project with an estimate and suggested setting aside a contingency for unstable material costs.
The committee used a per-square-foot figure to compare Ritter renovation and addition, Town Hall renovation, and TCP renovation, stressing these are not estimates.

budget_items.topic: Earlier TCP renovation and rebuild costs
budget_items.what_was_said: Members recalled prior TCP renovation and rebuild numbers including soft costs.

budget_items.topic: Design funding at a fall special town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: A member suggested the committee seek roughly a quarter million for design work at a special town meeting in the fall.
The board committed the quarterly water bills.
figures_as_heard: ten thousand sixty six dollars and eleven cents

budget_items.what_was_said: A regional transit authority rural transportation grant will fund subsidized rides, with fares by distance; a further grant opportunity for the town was mentioned.
The green committee said the town has received a large sum of free state money to date and wants projects to fund.

budget_items.topic: Public comment on community space cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident combined square footage figures into a total cost for community space.

budget_items.topic: Mortgage escrow increases from tax bills
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said some residents' monthly escrow payments jumped due to higher tax bills.

decisions.decision: Board members indicated the committee's next step should be a roadmap, and that funding for design would be the board's prerogative to pursue.
The school committee letter will be scanned and added to the Google Drive for discussion next week.
Town manager composite evaluation to be discussed next week; individual evaluations available in the town manager's office, and members must not reference their own evaluations in discussion.
Chair will explore a conversation with large local earth-removal businesses in early June about an RFP for site work in exchange for removal rights.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to deny the request of the residents at 243 Summer Street as presented.
The Municipal Building Design Committee presented a hybrid plan for Ritter, Town Hall and the old TCP building, with preliminary comparative costs it said are not estimates.
The board heard the consultant's report on waterfront land valuation, and a resident and members criticized the assessors' abatement process.
The board approved the fourth quarter water commitment and a Boys and Girls Club toll booth fundraiser.
The town manager's composite evaluation was deferred to next week.

why_it_matters: The building plan could lead to a design funding request at a fall special town meeting, which residents would be asked to vote on.
The abatement discussion touches how property assessments are corrected and how long residents wait for relief on their tax bills.
watch_next: The next Select Board meeting, where the town manager's composite evaluation and the school committee's sidewalk letter are due for discussion.
A possible design funding article at a fall special town meeting, if the Municipal Building Design Committee pursues the roadmap.
